title: Free time
grammar: Linking sentences: en, maar, of, want, dus
summary: en, maar, of and want stand outside the next sentence: normal order after them. After dus both orders are right (dus ik blijf, dus blijf ik). A comma before maar, want and dus.
explain:
Five short words join two sentences into one: `en` (and), `maar` (but), `of` (or), `want` (because) and `dus` (so). For four of them the word order is easy: they stand **outside** the second sentence, and that sentence keeps the order it would have on its own. `dus` is different, because it can also be part of the sentence.

### en, maar, of, want: nothing changes

The conjunction does not count as the first element of the second sentence (you will also see this called *position 0*). After it comes a complete sentence, with the verb in second place as usual.

| first sentence | link | second sentence |
| Ik ben moe | en | ik ga naar huis. |
| Ik wil wel | maar | ik heb geen tijd. |
| We gaan zwemmen | of | we gaan fietsen. |
| Ik blijf thuis | want | ik ben ziek. |

> Ik zing in een koor en mijn man speelt gitaar. — I sing in a choir and my husband plays the guitar.
> Ik train graag, maar ik ben niet fanatiek. — I like training, but I am not a fanatic.

When the second sentence starts with something other than the subject, it has inversion, exactly as it would on its own:

> Ons team heeft gewonnen, maar morgen spelen we weer. — Our team has won, but tomorrow we play again.

### want and omdat

Both give a reason. `want` joins two main clauses, so the order stays normal. `omdat` starts a sub-clause, and there the verb goes to the end (unit A2 · 23):

> Ik kom niet, want ik heb training. — I am not coming, because I have training.
> Ik kom niet, omdat ik training heb. — I am not coming, because I have training.

The part with `want` always comes second. A sentence never starts with it: not *Want ik heb training, ik kom niet.

### dus: three right orders

`dus` can be a conjunction, with normal order after it, or an adverb. As an adverb it can take the first place, and then the verb comes before the subject; or it can stand in the middle of the sentence. All of these are correct:

> Het regent, dus ik blijf thuis. — It is raining, so I am staying at home.
> Het regent, dus blijf ik thuis. — It is raining, so I am staying at home.
> Het regent. Ik blijf dus thuis. — It is raining. So I am staying at home.

### of: or

`of` joins two words or two sentences: `Wil je thee of koffie?`, `Ga je mee, of blijf je thuis?` (Later you will also meet `of` meaning "whether"; that is a different use.)

### Leaving out what is repeated

After `en`, `maar` and `of` you can leave out a subject that is the same in both parts, when the first sentence starts with that subject:

> Ik brei een trui en luister naar de radio. — I knit a jumper and listen to the radio.

With `ik` repeated (`en ik luister`) it is also correct. After `want` and `dus` the subject must stay: `…, dus ik blijf thuis`, never *dus blijf thuis.

### Commas

Put a comma before `maar`, `want` and `dus`. Before `en` and `of` there is normally no comma, except to make a long sentence easier to read.

### Watch out

- No inversion after want: `want ik ben moe`, not *want ben ik moe.
- Do not mix want and omdat: `want ik ben moe` or `omdat ik moe ben`, not *omdat ik ben moe.
- Do not drop the subject after want or dus.

### Compared with Ukrainian

Ukrainian `бо` works like `want`: it gives a reason and changes nothing in the order after it. The difference is that Dutch order is fixed: after these words comes a normal Dutch sentence, with its verb in second place.

sentences.nl: Ik zing in een koor en mijn man speelt gitaar.
sentences.en: I sing in a choir and my husband plays the guitar.
sentences.note: en does not count as the first element: after it comes a normal sentence, subject first, then the verb.

sentences.nl: Ik schilder graag, maar ik heb weinig tijd.
sentences.en: I like painting, but I have little time.
sentences.note: A comma before maar, and after it the normal order: ik heb.

sentences.nl: Mijn zoon is lid van een voetbalvereniging, want hij voetbalt graag.
sentences.en: My son is a member of a football club, because he likes playing football.
sentences.note: want gives a reason with normal order: hij voetbalt. With omdat the verb would go to the end: omdat hij graag voetbalt.

sentences.nl: We hebben vanavond training, dus ik kan niet komen.
sentences.en: We have training this evening, so I cannot come.
sentences.note: After dus both orders are right: dus ik kan, with dus as a conjunction, or dus kan ik, with dus in the first place.
alt: We hebben vanavond training, dus kan ik niet komen.
Vanavond hebben we training, dus ik kan niet komen.
Vanavond hebben we training, dus kan ik niet komen.

sentences.nl: Wil je liever tennissen of zwemmen?
sentences.en: Would you rather play tennis or go swimming?
sentences.note: of joins two words here, two infinitives at the end of the question. Liever is the comparative of graag.
alt: Wil jij liever tennissen of zwemmen?

sentences.nl: Ons team heeft gewonnen, maar morgen spelen we weer.
sentences.en: Our team has won, but tomorrow we play again.
sentences.note: After maar the second sentence starts with morgen, so it has inversion, as it would on its own: morgen spelen we.
alt: Ons team heeft gewonnen, maar we spelen morgen weer.

sentences.nl: Ik brei een trui en luister naar de radio.
sentences.en: I knit a jumper and listen to the radio.
sentences.note: Both parts have the same subject, and the sentence starts with it, so after en ik can be left out.
alt: Ik brei een trui en ik luister naar de radio.

sentences.nl: Hij is heel sportief, want hij traint vijf keer per week.
sentences.en: He is very sporty, because he trains five times a week.
sentences.note: want + normal order: hij traint. The subject cannot be left out after want.
alt: Hij is erg sportief, want hij traint vijf keer per week.

sentences.nl: Ik ben niet fanatiek, dus ik doe niet mee aan wedstrijden.
sentences.en: I am not a fanatic, so I do not take part in competitions.
sentences.note: dus as a conjunction keeps the normal order. Dus doe ik niet mee is just as right.
alt: Ik ben niet fanatiek, dus doe ik niet mee aan wedstrijden.

sentences.nl: De contributie is vrij hoog, maar de trainers zijn goed.
sentences.en: The membership fee is quite high, but the coaches are good.
sentences.note: maar joins two complete sentences, each with its own subject and verb, and a comma in front of maar.

exercises.nl: Tekenen is mijn hobby, ___ ik heb weinig tijd.
exercises.en: Drawing is my hobby, but I have little time.
exercises.note: The second part goes against the first, so maar. Want would give a reason and dus a result, and neither makes sense here.

exercises.nl: Ik ga vanavond niet naar het koor, ___ ik ben verkouden.
exercises.en: I am not going to the choir this evening, because I have a cold.
exercises.note: Being ill is the reason, so want. After want the order stays normal: ik ben.

exercises.nl: Ik kom niet naar de wedstrijd, want ___.
exercises.en: I am not coming to the match, because I have training.
exercises.note: want is outside the second sentence, so subject and verb keep their normal order. The verb at the end belongs to omdat.

exercises.nl: Ik kom niet naar de wedstrijd, omdat ___.
exercises.en: I am not coming to the match, because I have training.
exercises.note: omdat starts a sub-clause, and there the verb goes to the end: omdat ik training heb. That is the difference from want.

exercises.nl: Ik train elke dag, ___ ik wil de wedstrijd winnen.
answers: want
exercises.en: I train every day, because I want to win the match.
exercises.note: A reason with normal order after it (ik wil) is want. Omdat would need the verb at the end: omdat ik de wedstrijd wil winnen.

exercises.nl: Hij is ziek, ___ hij kan niet meedoen aan de wedstrijd.
answers: dus
exercises.en: He is ill, so he cannot take part in the match.
exercises.note: A result is dus. Here it is used as a conjunction, with normal order after it: hij kan.

exercises.nl: Gaan we zaterdag fietsen, ___ blijven we thuis?
answers: of
exercises.en: Are we going cycling on Saturday, or are we staying at home?
exercises.note: of = or. It joins two questions here; each keeps its own order with the verb first.

answers: Ik kom niet, want ik heb vanavond training.
Ik kom niet, want vanavond heb ik training.
exercises.en: I am not coming, because I have training this evening.
exercises.note: After want the second sentence has its own normal order: subject and verb, or vanavond first and then the verb before ik.

answers: Het regent, dus we trainen binnen.
Het regent, dus trainen we binnen.
exercises.en: It is raining, so we are training indoors.
exercises.note: dus allows both orders: as a conjunction with normal order (dus we trainen), or in the first place with the verb before the subject (dus trainen we).

answers: Vandaag heb ik geen tijd, maar morgen kom ik.
Vandaag heb ik geen tijd, maar ik kom morgen.
exercises.en: Today I have no time, but tomorrow I will come.
exercises.note: maar is outside the second sentence. If morgen comes first, the verb comes before ik; if ik comes first, the order is normal.

exercises.task: Join the two sentences with want.
exercises.from: Ik ga naar de training. Ik wil fitter worden.
answers: Ik ga naar de training, want ik wil fitter worden.
exercises.en: I am going to training, because I want to get fitter.
exercises.note: The two sentences stay as they are, with a comma and want in between. After want nothing in the order changes.

exercises.task: Join the two sentences with dus.
exercises.from: Mijn vriendin is fanatiek. Ze traint elke dag.
answers: Mijn vriendin is fanatiek, dus ze traint elke dag.
Mijn vriendin is fanatiek, dus zij traint elke dag.
Mijn vriendin is fanatiek, dus traint ze elke dag.
Mijn vriendin is fanatiek, dus traint zij elke dag.
exercises.en: My friend is a fanatic, so she trains every day.
exercises.note: Both orders are right after dus: dus ze traint (conjunction) and dus traint ze (dus in the first place).

exercises.task: Say it with omdat instead of want.
exercises.from: Ik ben lid van een klimclub, want ik vind klimmen spannend.
answers: Ik ben lid van een klimclub, omdat ik klimmen spannend vind.
exercises.en: I am a member of a climbing club, because I find climbing exciting.
exercises.note: omdat sends the verb to the end of its clause: omdat ik klimmen spannend vind. With want the verb stays in second place.

exercises.task: Leave out the subject that is repeated.
exercises.from: Mijn broer fotografeert graag en hij tekent ook.
answers: Mijn broer fotografeert graag en tekent ook.
exercises.en: My brother likes taking photographs and draws too.
exercises.note: After en the same subject can go when the first sentence starts with it. The verb tekent then follows en directly.

exercises.wrong: Ik ga niet mee, want ben ik moe.
answers: Ik ga niet mee, want ik ben moe.
exercises.en: I am not coming along, because I am tired.
exercises.note: want does not take a place in the sentence after it, so there is no inversion: want ik ben moe.

exercises.wrong: Mijn zus is ziek, dus komt vanavond niet.
answers: Mijn zus is ziek, dus ze komt vanavond niet.
Mijn zus is ziek, dus zij komt vanavond niet.
Mijn zus is ziek, dus komt ze vanavond niet.
Mijn zus is ziek, dus komt zij vanavond niet.
exercises.en: My sister is ill, so she is not coming this evening.
exercises.note: After dus the subject cannot be left out (after en it could: en komt vanavond niet). Both dus ze komt and dus komt ze are right.
